metadata.title: Volume, Capacity of Prisms and Time Zones
metadata.vcaa_description: Solve problems involving the volume and capacity of right prisms using appropriate units; solve problems involving duration and time zones.
metadata.target_mastery: Calculate the volume of right prisms using $V = Ah$, convert between volume ($\text{cm}^3, \text{m}^3$) and liquid capacity ($\text{mL}, \text{L}, \text{kL}$), and solve duration and Australian/global time zone problems.
prerequisites: Area of rectangles, triangles, and trapeziums (Section 7A)

key_vocabulary.definition: A 3D solid with two identical, parallel polygon bases (its uniform cross-section of area $A$) joined by rectangular side faces perpendicular to the base.

Volume is the amount of 3D space an object occupies (measured in $\text{mm}^3, \text{cm}^3, \text{m}^3$). Capacity is the amount of fluid a container can hold (measured in $\text{mL}, \text{L}, \text{kL}, \text{ML}$).
Standard time zones across Australia relative to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC): AWST (UTC$+8$), ACST (UTC$+9.5$), and AEST (UTC$+10$), plus Daylight Saving AEDT (UTC$+11$) and ACDT (UTC$+10.5$).

theory.title: Volume of Any Right Prism ($V = Ah$)
theory.explanation: Every right prism has a uniform cross-section (the shape you see if you slice the prism parallel to its base anywhere along its length). The volume $V$ of any right prism equals the area $A$ of its uniform cross-section multiplied by the perpendicular length or height $h$ connecting the two identical bases.
theory.formula_latex: V = Ah \quad \left(V_{\text{rect prism}} = lwh, \quad V_{\text{triangular prism}} = \frac{1}{2}bh \times L\right)
theory.callout_rule: The base $A$ of a prism is NOT always the face resting on the ground — it is the two-dimensional face that stays identical when sliced parallel to the ends.

theory.title: Converting Volume Units and Linking Volume to Capacity
theory.explanation: Because volume is three-dimensional, linear conversion factors are cubed: $1\text{ cm}^3 = 10^3\text{ mm}^3 = 1000\text{ mm}^3$ and $1\text{ m}^3 = 100^3\text{ cm}^3 = 1\,000\,000\text{ cm}^3$. By metric definition, $1\text{ cm}^3$ holds exactly $1\text{ mL}$ of liquid, a $10\text{ cm} \times 10\text{ cm} \times 10\text{ cm}$ cube ($1000\text{ cm}^3$) holds $1\text{ L}$, and $1\text{ m}^3$ holds $1000\text{ L} = 1\text{ kilolitre (kL)}$.
theory.formula_latex: 1\text{ cm}^3 = 1\text{ mL}, \qquad 1000\text{ cm}^3 = 1\text{ L}, \qquad 1\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ L} = 1\text{ kL}
theory.callout_title: Three Key Bridges Between Volume and Capacity
theory.callout_rule: Memorise: $1\text{ cm}^3 = 1\text{ mL}$ and $1\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ L} = 1\text{ kL}$.

theory.title: 24-Hour Time, Duration, and Australian Time Zones
theory.explanation: In standard winter time, Australia has three main time zones: Australian Western Standard Time (AWST, UTC$+8$: WA), Australian Central Standard Time (ACST, UTC$+9.5$: SA, NT), and Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST, UTC$+10$: VIC, NSW, QLD, TAS, ACT). During Daylight Saving (October–April), VIC, NSW, TAS, and ACT move $1$ hour forward to AEDT (UTC$+11$), and SA moves to ACDT (UTC$+10.5$), while WA, NT, and QLD do not observe Daylight Saving.
theory.callout_title: East is Ahead; West is Behind
theory.callout_rule: When converting from a western city (e.g., Perth) to an eastern city (e.g., Melbourne), ADD the time difference. Always convert flight departure and arrival to the SAME time zone before finding flight duration.

worked_examples.title: Calculating the Volume of a Triangular Prism
worked_examples.problem: A right triangular prism has a triangular cross-section with base $b = 12\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular triangle height $h_t = 9\text{ cm}$, and a prism length of $L = 20\text{ cm}$. Find (a) the cross-sectional area $A$, and (b) the volume $V$ of the prism in $\text{cm}^3$ and in litres ($\text{L}$).

steps.thinking: Calculate the area $A$ of the triangular cross-section using $A = \frac{1}{2}bh_t$.
Multiply $A$ by the prism length $L = 20\text{ cm}$ to find the volume in $\text{cm}^3$, then divide by $1000$ to convert $\text{cm}^3$ to litres.

now_you_try.problem: A triangular prism has a triangular cross-section of base $8\text{ cm}$ and height $5\text{ cm}$, and a prism length of $15\text{ cm}$. Find its volume in $\text{cm}^3$ and in $\text{mL}$.
now_you_try.hint: Find $A = \frac{1}{2}(8)(5) = 20\text{ cm}^2$, multiply by $15$, and use $1\text{ cm}^3 = 1\text{ mL}$.

worked_examples.title: Volume and Capacity of a Trapezoidal Swimming Pool
worked_examples.problem: A rectangular swimming pool is $25\text{ m}$ long and $10\text{ m}$ wide. Its depth slopes uniformly from $1.2\text{ m}$ at the shallow end to $2.4\text{ m}$ at the deep end, so its side profile is a trapezium. Find (a) the volume of the pool in $\text{m}^3$ and (b) its capacity in litres ($\text{L}$).

steps.thinking: The uniform cross-section is the trapezoidal side wall with parallel vertical depths $a = 1.2\text{ m}$ and $b = 2.4\text{ m}$ separated by the $25\text{ m}$ length.
Multiply the cross-sectional area $A = 45\text{ m}^2$ by the pool width $h = 10\text{ m}$, then multiply by $1000$ since $1\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ L}$.

now_you_try.problem: A water trough has a trapezoidal cross-section with parallel top and bottom widths $60\text{ cm}$ and $40\text{ cm}$, perpendicular depth $30\text{ cm}$, and length $200\text{ cm}$. Find its capacity in litres.
now_you_try.hint: Find $A = \frac{1}{2}(60 + 40) \times 30\text{ cm}^2$, multiply by $200\text{ cm}$, and divide by $1000$.

worked_examples.title: Calculating Flight Arrivals Across Australian Time Zones
worked_examples.problem: In January (during Daylight Saving), Melbourne is on AEDT (UTC$+11$) and Perth is on AWST (UTC$+8$). A Qantas flight departs Melbourne at $10{:}45\text{ am}$ AEDT and takes $4\text{ hours } 20\text{ minutes}$. At what local time (AWST) does the flight land in Perth?

steps.thinking: First find the arrival time in Melbourne time (AEDT) by adding the flight duration of $4\text{ h } 20\text{ min}$ to $10{:}45\text{ am}$.
Perth (UTC$+8$) is $11 - 8 = 3$ hours behind Melbourne (UTC$+11$). Subtract $3$ hours from $15{:}05$.

now_you_try.problem: On the same January day, a return flight departs Perth at $1{:}30\text{ pm}$ AWST (UTC$+8$) and flies for $3\text{ hours } 45\text{ minutes}$ to Melbourne (AEDT, UTC$+11$). What is the local arrival time in Melbourne?
now_you_try.hint: Add $3\text{ h } 45\text{ min}$ to $13{:}30$, then add $3\text{ hours}$ for the time zone change.

common_misconceptions.title: Equating $1\text{ m}^3$ to $100\text{ L}$ Instead of $1000\text{ L}$
common_misconceptions.misconception: Thinking $1\text{ m}^3 = 100\text{ L}$ because $1\text{ m} = 100\text{ cm}$.
common_misconceptions.correct_concept: A $1\text{ m} \times 1\text{ m} \times 1\text{ m}$ cube holds $10 \times 10 \times 10 = 1000$ one-litre cubes (each $10\text{ cm} \times 10\text{ cm} \times 10\text{ cm}$), so $1\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ L} = 1\text{ kL}$.

common_misconceptions.title: Treating Minutes as Base-100 Decimals ($1.5\text{ hours} \neq 1\text{ h } 50\text{ min}$)
common_misconceptions.misconception: Interpreting $2.5\text{ hours}$ as $2\text{ hours } 50\text{ minutes}$ or subtracting times as standard base-$10$ numbers.
common_misconceptions.correct_concept: There are $60$ minutes in $1$ hour, so $0.5\text{ hours} = 0.5 \times 60 = 30\text{ minutes}$, and $0.25\text{ hours} = 15\text{ minutes}$.
common_misconceptions.counter_example: Half an hour is $30$ minutes, not $50$ minutes.

fluency_and_understanding.question: Calculate the volume in $\text{cm}^3$ and capacity in litres ($\text{L}$) of a rectangular fish tank measuring $60\text{ cm}$ long, $30\text{ cm}$ wide, and $40\text{ cm}$ high.
step_by_step_solution: Multiply the three dimensions: $V = lwh = 60 \times 30 \times 40 = 72\,000\text{ cm}^3$.
Divide by $1000$ to convert $\text{cm}^3$ to litres: $72\,000 \div 1000 = 72\text{ L}$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: Convert: (a) $4.2\text{ m}^3$ to litres ($\text{L}$), and (b) $8500\text{ cm}^3$ to litres ($\text{L}$).
step_by_step_solution: Since $1\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ L}$, $4.2\text{ m}^3 = 4.2 \times 1000 = 4200\text{ L}$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: A right prism has an L-shaped cross-sectional area of $42\text{ cm}^2$ and a length of $15\text{ cm}$. Calculate its volume.
step_by_step_solution: Use the prism volume formula $V = Ah$ with $A = 42\text{ cm}^2$ and $h = 15\text{ cm}$.
Multiply: $V = 42 \times 15 = 630\text{ cm}^3$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: A right triangular prism has a volume of $540\text{ cm}^3$ and a length of $18\text{ cm}$. If the base of its triangular cross-section is $10\text{ cm}$, find the perpendicular height $h_t$ of the triangle.
step_by_step_solution: First find the cross-sectional area $A = \frac{V}{L} = \frac{540}{18} = 30\text{ cm}^2$.
Substitute into the triangle area formula $30 = \frac{1}{2}(10)h_t = 5h_t \implies h_t = 6\text{ cm}$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: In June (standard time), Adelaide is on ACST (UTC$+9.5$) and Brisbane is on AEST (UTC$+10$). When a live AFL match kicks off in Adelaide at $7{:}10\text{ pm}$ ACST, what is the local time in (a) Brisbane (AEST) and (b) Perth (AWST, UTC$+8$)?
step_by_step_solution: Brisbane (UTC$+10$) is $0.5$ hours ($30$ minutes) ahead of Adelaide (UTC$+9.5$), giving $7{:}10\text{ pm} + 30\text{ min} = 7{:}40\text{ pm}$ AEST.
Perth (UTC$+8$) is $1.5$ hours ($1\text{ h } 30\text{ min}$) behind Adelaide (UTC$+9.5$), giving $7{:}10\text{ pm} - 1\text{ h } 30\text{ min} = 5{:}40\text{ pm}$ AWST.

fluency_and_understanding.question: A V/Line train departs Southern Cross Station at $08{:}48$ and arrives in Warrnambool at $12{:}23$ on the same day. How long is the journey in hours and minutes?
step_by_step_solution: Count forward from $08{:}48$ to $09{:}00$ ($12\text{ minutes}$), then from $09{:}00$ to $12{:}00$ ($3\text{ hours}$), plus $23\text{ minutes}$ to $12{:}23$.
Add the parts: $3\text{ hours} + (12 + 23)\text{ minutes} = 3\text{ hours } 35\text{ minutes}$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: A rectangular house roof in Ballarat has a horizontal footprint area of $180\text{ m}^2$. During a storm, $25\text{ mm}$ ($0.025\text{ m}$) of rain falls uniformly across the roof and drains into a rainwater tank with no loss. How many litres of water enter the tank?
step_by_step_solution: Calculate the volume of water in cubic metres: $V = Ah = 180\text{ m}^2 \times 0.025\text{ m} = 4.5\text{ m}^3$.
Convert $\text{m}^3$ to litres by multiplying by $1000$: $4.5 \times 1000 = 4500\text{ L}$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: A concrete driveway slab is $12\text{ m}$ long, $3.5\text{ m}$ wide, and $15\text{ cm}$ ($0.15\text{ m}$) thick. Ready-mix concrete costs $\$280$ per cubic metre. Calculate (a) the volume of concrete required in $\text{m}^3$ and (b) the total cost of the concrete.
step_by_step_solution: Convert all dimensions to metres and multiply: $V = 12 \times 3.5 \times 0.15 = 6.3\text{ m}^3$.
Multiply volume by $\$280/\text{m}^3$: $6.3 \times 280 = \$1764$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: An international flight departs Melbourne (AEDT, UTC$+11$) at $11{:}30\text{ pm}$ on Tuesday and arrives in Singapore (SGT, UTC$+8$) at $4{:}15\text{ am}$ SGT on Wednesday. Find the flight duration in hours and minutes.
step_by_step_solution: Convert the departure time to Singapore time (UTC$+8$ is $3$ hours behind UTC$+11$): $11{:}30\text{ pm} - 3\text{ hours} = 8{:}30\text{ pm}$ SGT on Tuesday.

Find the elapsed time from $8{:}30\text{ pm}$ Tuesday to $4{:}15\text{ am}$ Wednesday: $3\text{ h } 30\text{ min}$ to midnight plus $4\text{ h } 15\text{ min}$ after midnight $= 7\text{ hours } 45\text{ minutes}$.

reasoning_and_communication.question: A triangular tent is $2.4\text{ m}$ long, with a triangular front opening of base $1.8\text{ m}$ and height $1.5\text{ m}$. A student says the 'base' of the tent is the $2.4\text{ m} \times 1.8\text{ m}$ rectangular floor and multiplies that area by $1.5\text{ m}$. Explain why this is wrong and calculate the correct volume.
reasoning_and_communication.final_answer: The rectangular floor is not a uniform cross-section because the tent narrows to a ridge at the top; correct volume is $V = \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 1.8 \times 1.5\right) \times 2.4 = 3.24\text{ m}^3$
step_by_step_solution: Slices parallel to the rectangular floor shrink as you move upwards towards the top ridge, whereas slices parallel to the triangular front stay identical along the $2.4\text{ m}$ length.
Using the triangular cross-section $A = \frac{1}{2}(1.8)(1.5) = 1.35\text{ m}^2$ gives the true volume $V = 1.35 \times 2.4 = 3.24\text{ m}^3$ (half the student's answer of $6.48\text{ m}^3$).

reasoning_and_communication.question: During Daylight Saving in January, why is Brisbane (QLD) $1$ hour behind Sydney (NSW) even though both cities lie at nearly the same longitude on Australia's east coast?
reasoning_and_communication.final_answer: New South Wales advances its clocks by $1$ hour to AEDT (UTC$+11$) in summer, whereas Queensland remains on standard time AEST (UTC$+10$) all year round
step_by_step_solution: Time zones follow state/territory legislation as well as longitude.
In summer, NSW observes Daylight Saving Time (AEDT, UTC$+11$) while Queensland stays on Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST, UTC$+10$), creating a $1$-hour difference.

reasoning_and_communication.question: If every linear dimension (length, width, and height) of a rectangular prism is multiplied by a scale factor of $k = 3$, by what factor does (a) its surface area increase and (b) its volume increase? Prove your answer algebraically.
reasoning_and_communication.final_answer: (a) Surface area increases by a factor of $3^2 = 9$; (b) volume increases by a factor of $3^3 = 27$
step_by_step_solution: Replacing $l, w, h$ with $3l, 3w, 3h$ in each rectangular face area multiplies every face area by $3 \times 3 = 9$.
In the volume formula, $V_{\text{new}} = (3l)(3w)(3h) = 27lwh = 27V$, so the volume increases by $3^3 = 27$.
